title: Consumption Scenario Simulator and Preset Generator — Design Spec
author: Maya Chen
summary: This design spec describes the Consumption Scenario Simulator (CSS): a deterministic simulation engine and preset generator used by Solutions Engineering, Onboarding, and Sales to produce reproducible cost, latency, and quality tradeoff projections and exportable consumption presets. The CSS enables side-by-side comparisons across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes and produces artifacts that can be imported into Console and Optimize for automated configuration.
overview: Problem: Customers and internal teams need concise, defensible answers to the question: 'What will this workload cost and how should we configure the runtime for the target latency and budget?' The CSS addresses this by combining model performance profiles, infra pricing, and workload shape to generate estimates and ranked consumption presets. Scope: simulator engine, preset ranking rules, API, Console integration, report and preset export. Out of scope: contract negotiation, invoice generation, and billing enforcement systems.
primary_users: Solutions Engineers, Onboarding, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, Product Managers
primary_use_cases: 1) Rapid pre-sales TCO comparisons across deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private). 2) Onboarding recommendations: produce a recommended preset that balances customer budget and latency SLO. 3) Sensitivity analysis: vary batch sizes, cache-hit rates, or quantization to show marginal impact. 4) Export a YAML preset that can be automatically applied or validated in a canary run.
design_principles: Deterministic: runs are reproducible given a seed and spec. Fast: quick-preview responses in seconds for common cases; full-calibration runs targeted to complete within minutes. Explainable: every recommended knob must include an impact statement. Calibrated: draws from live telemetry and model catalog. Conservative-by-default: recommendations include risk tiers (conservative, balanced, experimental).
architecture_high_level: Components: API layer (/v1/consumption-scenarios), job orchestrator (serverless job or batch worker), runner container (simulation logic + cost model), preset ranking engine (rules + scoring), artifact storage (object store) and metadata DB. Telemetry: emit run-level metrics for observability and model drift detection. Integrations: model-catalog (latency/cost profiles), telemetry-query (recent p50/p95), infra-pricing-catalog.
api_contracts: POST /v1/consumption-scenarios -> accepts a scenario_spec and returns run_id and status. GET /v1/consumption-scenarios/{run_id} -> returns report URLs and summary. POST /v1/consumption-scenarios/{run_id}/apply-preset -> optional internal-only call that triggers a canary application. Inputs are validated and stored with hashed identifiers for privacy.
preset_yaml_example:
name: onboard-balanced
batching:
  target_batch_size: 12
  max_latency_ms: 35
cache:
  kv_cache_enabled: true
  prefix_hit_rate: 0.32
quantization:
  profile: int8-balanced
routing:
  preferred_tier: dedicated_high_io
rollout:
  canary_percent: 5
  monitor_window_minutes: 30
validation_table:
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| seed | int | yes | For reproducible runs; must be >0 |
| deployment_mode | enum | yes | hosted | dedicated | private |
| duration_hours | int | yes | 1-168 hours recommended |
| qps_profile | list | yes | hourly buckets or synthetic distribution |
| avg_tokens_in | int | yes | 1-10000 |
| avg_tokens_out | int | yes | 1-10000 |
| fidelity_target | string | optional | human-readable SLA parsed by heuristics |
| allowed_models | list | optional | pattern matching against model catalog |
